tagline: Turn cURL commands into idiomatic PHP — Guzzle, ext-curl, or zero-dependency streams
pageDescription: Free cURL to PHP converter transforms cURL commands into production-ready PHP using GuzzleHttp\Client, the native ext-curl extension, or file_get_contents with stream contexts. Handles method, headers, query parameters, JSON and form bodies, basic authentication, timeouts, and SSL verification. Perfect for PHP developers translating API documentation, Chrome DevTools exports, or Postman requests into runnable Laravel, Symfony, or plain-PHP code. Browser-based conversion means your cURL command never leaves your device — no signup, no server, no logs.

instructions.title: How to use cURL to PHP Converter

steps.title: Paste your cURL command
steps.description: Copy a cURL command from your terminal, browser DevTools, API docs, or Postman and paste it into the input area. The parser handles all common flags: -X, -H, -d, -u, --data-raw, --compressed, --max-time, and more.

steps.title: Pick the PHP flavor
steps.description: Choose Guzzle for modern Laravel/Symfony projects, native cURL for zero-dependency scripts on any PHP install with ext-curl, or file_get_contents for the simplest possible request with zero external dependencies.

steps.title: Copy the generated PHP
steps.description: The converter emits ready-to-run PHP with proper error handling, response parsing, and composer dependencies when applicable. Paste it straight into a controller, artisan command, or standalone script.

steps.title: Adjust error handling and options
steps.description: Tweak error handling mode, timeout, SSL verification, and comment density via the Options panel. The generator respects every toggle and emits the minimum idiomatic code for your preferences.

Use Guzzle for any project with Composer — best error handling and async support
Use native cURL when you cannot install Composer (shared hosting, legacy LAMP)
file_get_contents is great for quick smoke tests but cannot capture response headers or status codes robustly
Set timeout explicitly on any production request — PHP's default is too permissive
When calling internal APIs only, disable SSL verify only on local dev — never in production
troubleshooting: Guzzle class not found: run 'composer require guzzlehttp/guzzle' in your project
cURL function undefined: enable the 'curl' extension in php.ini (ext-curl)
file_get_contents returns false: enable 'allow_url_fopen' in php.ini and check SSL cert validity
Body not included in output: make sure -d or --data flags are properly quoted in the source cURL
Special characters mangled: source cURL must be UTF-8; escape single quotes in your payload
